greeting: In the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Spirit. Grace and peace be with you from God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ, who gathers us today in the light of His truth.
penitential:
Lord Jesus, you are the wisdom of God: Lord, have mercy.
Christ Jesus, you are the key of knowledge: Christ, have mercy.
Lord Jesus, you are the light that no darkness can overcome: Lord, have mercy.
psalm_response: The Lord has made known his salvation.
homily:
We often think of wisdom as a collection of facts—a library of information we can store away, a set of blueprints for how a life should be built. We imagine that if we just hold the right keys, if we just unlock the right doors, we can master the mystery of our days. But in today’s Gospel, Jesus offers a sharper, more piercing vision. He speaks to those who hold the keys of knowledge and warns them that they have not only failed to enter themselves, but have stood in the way of others. It is a sobering image: a door meant to be an entrance, now acting as a barrier.

Think of a key. A key is a small, unassuming piece of metal, yet it holds the power to change everything. It can open a home, a gate, or a cockpit. It is meant to be used, to be turned, to be given away. But a key that is hoarded, a key that is kept in a pocket and never put into the lock, becomes nothing more than a weight. It becomes a burden that clutters the heart. Jesus is calling us to a different kind of wisdom—one that doesn't just know the way, but walks it. He is calling us to stop trying to control the mystery of our lives and start living within the grace of it.

St. Paul, in his letter to the Ephesians, gives us the antidote to that hoarding. He speaks of a plan for the fullness of times, a plan where God 'has lavished upon us' every spiritual blessing. Notice that word: lavished. It is not a measured, careful distribution. It is an abundance that overflows. It is the kind of love that doesn't count the cost, but simply pours itself out. Paul reminds us that we were chosen 'before the foundation of the world, to be holy and without blemish.' This is not a goal we reach by our own effort; it is a gift we receive by our adoption into the family of God. We are not builders of our own salvation; we are children of the One who has already built a home for us.

Benjamin Vo lived as if he understood this mystery of the 'lavished' gift. He was a boy who knew that the most important things in life were not the things you could lock away in a safe, but the things you could share. Think of that moment when he offered his entire piggy bank to help his uncle. He didn't need to break it, he didn't need to empty it, he didn't need to tell the world. The offer itself was the truth of his heart. It was a secret, interior movement of love. It was a sign that Benjamin understood, better than most adults, that our value is not in what we keep, but in what we are willing to offer. He was a boy whose heart was not a vault, but a well—a well that kept giving, a well that kept flowing.

Alan and Thao, I know that for these four months, the silence of your home has been a heavy companion. You remember the way Ben would come to you with his ideas, his plans, his gentle smile. You remember the way he would listen—truly listen—to the stories his dad would tell, finding joy in the simple, quiet connection of a father and son. That bond is not a thing of the past. It is a living, breathing reality. It is the 'fullness of times' that Paul speaks of. It is the place where all of our loves are gathered and kept safe, beyond the reach of time or change. You are a family of four, and that is a truth that death cannot touch, because it is anchored in the promise of the One who is the Resurrection and the Life. You are not being asked to carry the weight of the past; you are being asked to walk into the future with the promise of the Resurrection as your light.

I want to speak very gently to the ache that visits you in the quiet of the night. There is a weight that parents often carry, a stone of wondering if they missed something, if they could have done more, if they could have changed the outcome. I want to lift that stone from you today. You were the parents Benjamin needed. You were his sanctuary. You were the ones who nurtured that brilliant, curious, gentle spirit. You did not miss anything. God does not look at your son’s life and find it lacking, and He does not look at your care for him and find it wanting. You are not being accused. You are being held. Let that stone fall. You are free to grieve, you are free to miss him, but you are not required to carry the burden of self-reproach. That is a weight that has no place in the kingdom of God. You are loved without limit, and you are being held by the same hands that hold him.

Ryan, you are a brother who knows the secret language of that love. You know that Ben is not gone; he has simply gone ahead to the place where all the 'con chim airlines' finally take flight. You are the one who carries the legacy of his curiosity, his kindness, and his smile. When you sit down to code, or when you look up at the clouds, know that you are not doing it alone. You are a family of four, and that bond is stronger than death. Keep being the boy who reaches out. Keep being the brother who knows that the most important things in life are not the things we possess, but the love we share. You are a witness to the fact that love is the only thing that actually lasts.

Look at the Gospel again. Jesus speaks of the 'key of knowledge' that has been taken away. He is warning us against the pride of thinking we have the final word on God’s plan. The scribes and Pharisees were so busy protecting their own understanding of the law that they missed the Lawgiver standing right in front of them. We do that, too. We try to understand the 'why' of our suffering, we try to map out the 'how' of our future, and we get so tangled in our own questions that we stop seeing the Presence. But the Presence is here. It is in the quiet of this room. It is in the ache of your heart. It is in the memory of a son who loved you with his whole life.

Think of the 'Well of Love' in Vietnam. That well is a perfect image of what you are doing. You are taking the love that was poured into Ben, and you are letting it flow into the lives of others. You are ensuring that his life is not a closed chapter, but a living, breathing, life-sustaining force. Every time you are kind, every time you choose to hope in the face of despair, you are allowing his legacy to refresh the world. You are turning the soil of the earth so that the Kingdom can grow. You are the ones who are keeping his light burning in a world that so often forgets to look up.

There is a profound freedom in realizing that we do not have to hold it all together. We do not have to be the ones who provide the answers. We are children of the freeborn woman. We are heirs to a kingdom that is not built by human hands, but by the grace of God. That grace is the 'bread' we need for the journey. It is the strength that comes when our own strength is gone. It is the peace that settles over us when we finally stop fighting the silence and start listening to the voice of the Father.

So today, carry this away with you: you are never alone. You are a family that is being held by the same hands that hold the universe. When you see a bird in flight, or a plane climbing into the clouds, don't just see a machine or a creature; see a sign of the freedom that Benjamin now knows. See a sign of the promise that you are walking toward. Keep your eyes on the horizon. The journey is not over; it is simply continuing in a new, more glorious way. And one day, when the long road reaches the end, you will look up and see him waiting for you, and the joy will be beyond all reckoning.

Take this with you: you are a family of four, and that will never change. The geography of your life has shifted, but the bond of your love is eternal. Keep the 'Well of Love' flowing in his name. Keep the kindness moving. Keep the dream alive. And when you walk out those doors, look up at the sky. Remember that he is not in the dust. He is in the light. He is waiting for you, and he is watching over you with that same sweet, gentle smile that you remember so vividly. That smile is a sign. It is a sign that the harvest is coming, and that the One who started this good work in you will surely bring it to completion. You are loved without limit, and you are being held by the same hands that hold him. Amen.
standing_petitions: For our beloved Ben and all who have gone before us, that they may rest forever in the radiant light of Christ.
For all who are grieving, that God may console them with His peace and fill their hearts with the hope of the Resurrection.
spiritual_communion: My Jesus, I believe that You are present in the Most Holy Sacrament. I love You above all things, and I desire to receive You into my soul. Since I cannot at this moment receive You sacramentally, come at least spiritually into my heart. I embrace You as if You were already there and unite myself wholly to You. Never permit me to be separated from You. Amen.
closing: May the Lord bless you and keep you, may He let His face shine upon you and be gracious to you, and may He give you His peace. In the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Spirit. Amen.

readings.label: Reading 1
readings.text:
Paul, an Apostle of Christ Jesus by the will of God,
to the holy ones who are in Ephesus
and faithful in Christ Jesus:
grace to you and peace from God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ.Blessed be the God and Father of our Lord Jesus Christ,
who has blessed us in Christ
with every spiritual blessing in the heavens,
as he chose us in him, before the foundation of the world,
to be holy and without blemish before him.
In love he destined us for adoption to himself through Jesus Christ,
in accord with the favor of his will,
for the praise of the glory of his grace
that he granted us in the beloved.In Christ we have redemption by his Blood,
the forgiveness of transgressions,
in accord with the riches of his grace that he lavished upon us.
In all wisdom and insight, he has made known to us
the mystery of his will in accord with his favor
that he set forth in him as a plan for the fullness of times,
to sum up all things in Christ, in heaven and on earth.

readings.label: Responsorial Psalm
readings.text:
R. (2a) The Lord has made known his salvation.
Sing to the LORD a new song,
for he has done wondrous deeds;
His right hand has won victory for him,
his holy arm.
R. The Lord has made known his salvation.
The LORD has made his salvation known:
in the sight of the nations he has revealed his justice.
He has remembered his kindness and his faithfulness
toward the house of Israel.
R. The Lord has made known his salvation.
All the ends of the earth have seen
the salvation by our God.
Sing joyfully to the LORD, all you lands;
break into song; sing praise.
R. The Lord has made known his salvation.
Sing praise to the LORD with the harp,
with the harp and melodious song.
With trumpets and the sound of the horn
sing joyfully before the King, the LORD.
R. The Lord has made known his salvation.

readings.label: Gospel
readings.text:
The Lord said:
“Woe to you who build the memorials of the prophets 
whom your fathers killed.
Consequently, you bear witness and give consent
to the deeds of your ancestors,
for they killed them and you do the building.
Therefore, the wisdom of God said,
‘I will send to them prophets and Apostles;
some of them they will kill and persecute’
in order that this generation might be charged
with the blood of all the prophets
shed since the foundation of the world,
from the blood of Abel to the blood of Zechariah
who died between the altar and the temple building.
Yes, I tell you, this generation will be charged with their blood!
Woe to you, scholars of the law!
You have taken away the key of knowledge.
You yourselves did not enter and you stopped those trying to enter.”
When Jesus left, the scribes and Pharisees
began to act with hostility toward him
and to interrogate him about many things,
for they were plotting to catch him at something he might say.

pet_prayers.text: Ben ơi, trong giấc ngủ anh Huy đã thấy Ben về thăm anh, trao cho anh lời cầu nguyện để hai anh em mình lại được tìm thấy nhau. Xin Chúa thương nhậm lời Ben, cho Ben được hưởng ngàn thu bình an bên Chúa. Nếu có thể, xin Ben lại ghé thăm anh trong những giấc mơ tiếp theo nhé, dù chỉ là một lời chào hay một nụ cười thân thương như ngày nào.

pet_prayers.name: Dad
pet_prayers.text: Ben, my sweet boy, I miss you so much. Thank you for visiting me and Chú Chris last night. He told me he saw you flying a helicopter—so free, joyful, and strong up there. Down here, Mom and I are crying more and more each day. A piece of my heart feels completely dead without you, Ben. Please watch over us, pray for your mom, your brother Ryan, and me, and give us the strength to keep going. We love you forever

pet_prayers.name: Dad
pet_prayers.text: Today marks 100 days without you. Miss you a whole a lot Ben. Feel free to visit any time! See you around buddy! Love you!

Ben ơi, nay anh M đi xử lý hồ sơ ở Cam Ranh, đi ngang qua Cam Ranh Airport. Rồi cuộc nói chuyện về máy bay của Ben lại ùa về, nhớ nhiều kỷ niệm về Ben lắm ( anh M sẽ giữ kín kakaka). Quỷ nhỏ, tự nhiên nghĩ về mày buồn dễ sợ. Hãy đi đến những nơi mà Ben muốn nha và đừng quên là luôn nhớ về gia đình mình nhé, thương em trai nhiều. Giá như !!!!!!!!!

pet_prayers.name: Dad
pet_prayers.text: What happened my son? It's been 3 months since you left us. Missing you so much my whole body aches. Mom cries every day now... What are we going to do now Ben?  Please pray for us.

pet_prayers.name: Dad
pet_prayers.text:
Hey Ben,

Rafael Rizzo and his little brother Ben really need your help right now. Please bless them with good health and give them the strength to get through this together. Please watch over Brandon and Flor's health, too.

I miss you a whole bunch. I know you're up in heaven watching over all of us. Whenever you're able to, stop by to visit, yeah? I love you and miss you so much!

pet_prayers.name: Dad
pet_prayers.text:
Hey Ben - Miss you a whole bunch. Crying all day yesterday, i hope today will be better. Please guide our family through this grief... There's a 14 year old boy that just left earth on August 12... His name is Phero Aden Vo - look for him, maybe you guys can be friends...

Please pray for me and mom to have good health and strength.

I love and miss you Ben
